The shares were trading near $334.68 at the time of writing, up 2.88% over the past week, ahead of the bank's earnings report.

Based on the at-the-money $335 strike expiring Oct. 16, the options market is pricing in a post-earnings move of about 2.84% in either direction. Using the adjusted combined call and put premium of $9.52, this implies an expected trading range of roughly $325.16 to $344.20 following the results.

For the Oct. 16 weekly expiration, the $345 call has the highest open interest, at 7,220 contracts, while the $330 put leads on the put side with 3,892 contracts. These strikes sit near the stock's current price and mark key concentrations of outstanding weekly options positions.
Moreover, trading activity favored calls, with 13,180 call contracts versus 9,191 put contracts, giving a put/call volume ratio of 0.70.
While open interest showed a similar tilt with 75,452 call contracts versus 41,243 put contracts, resulting in a put/call open-interest ratio of 0.55.
Looking across all expirations, the $360 call holds the highest call open interest, at 31,994 contracts, while the $300 put leads on the put side with 23,837 contracts.

Meanwhile, JPMorgan's at-the-money implied volatility stands at 40.25%, well above its historical volatility of 16.31%. The gap indicates that options are pricing in greater near-term volatility than reflected in the historical measure ahead of the earnings announcement.
